no_index_reason: No index is published for this country. The Monitored-Area ESDI's sector weights, decay horizons and transmission measure were built for a strike campaign and do not transfer (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §1-§3). This view shows reported major disruptions and energy-system context instead.

sectors.reason: Denominator ready: Aramco's annual report lists all nine in-Kingdom refineries (gross basis). Four are joint ventures, so numerator and denominator must come from the same gross rows. Not scored. The recovery and decay model behind the Monitored-Area ESDI was calibrated on repeated strikes with almost no restart reporting, and no model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).

reporting_environment_text: Disruption is disclosed mainly through company and ministry statements, usually only when material to investors or the state.
reporting_note: Aramco discloses disruption at the level of financial materiality; the energy ministry issues statements after attacks. There is no event register, so the coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: 13 regions (ISO SA-01 to SA-14; there is no SA-13). Official electricity statistics are reported by four operating areas, not these regions.

rulings.note: Includes the Saudi share of the former Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

campaigns.name: Attacks on Saudi energy facilities, 2026
campaigns.status_basis: Attacks on Saudi energy facilities were still being reported in late October 2026, and no ceasefire was found (independent review, 2026-10-31).

release_rule.text: Facility-specific restart, recovery or operating status for a record in a campaign is published only once the campaign is recorded as ended and 30 days have passed. While it is active the event itself is published; its facility status is not.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-10-30 by the Saudi Arabia source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read from the cited document in this session; mixed vintages (2022-2025) are stated per row and must not be combined into one 'current' picture. Bases differ by source (country totals from EIA; company totals from Aramco; grid-connected capacity from SEC) and are labelled on each row. OPEC, Energy Institute and Saudi government sites were not machine-readable on this date, so no figure is taken from them. See docs/countries/SA_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

significance: Crude oil and other petroleum liquids made up 85% of Saudi Arabia's primary energy production in 2022 and natural gas 15%, with no coal production (EIA).
Saudi Arabia meets all of its natural gas consumption with domestic production (EIA, 2024).
In 2023 an estimated 62% of Saudi electricity was generated from natural gas and 38% from oil, with renewables under 1% (EIA).

Aramco reports five wholly-owned and four affiliated refineries in the Kingdom, which together accounted for 63% of its 4.2 million b/d net refining capacity at the end of 2025 (Aramco Annual Report 2025).

The record is dominated by conflict episodes (March 2022, and 2026). That reflects how Saudi incidents are reported, not the absence of other disruption.

research_log.note: What was searched, when, and how far it got. Counts only: the candidate queue's per-record narratives are kept off the public record (data/candidates/README.md). A TARGETED pass chases named gaps and leads; a SYSTEMATIC pass declares its source lanes and window before searching, and is complete only when every lane was executed. A window searched with the budget exhausted is PARTIAL, not researched-and-quiet.

lanes.limitation: Nothing was searched or read in this pass: all ten declared queries were refused by the shared search limit (five attempted, none performed), and SPA (HTTP 403) and the ministry site (no response) refused ordinary access once each. The four English year queries for 2022-2025 have still never been run in any pass.

lanes.source_family: Saudi Aramco disclosures: Tadawul announcements; aramco.com news and annual-report incident statements
lanes.finding: All four annual reports (FY2022-FY2025) were read in English. No report mentions the March 2022 YASREF event already in the corpus, or any fire, unplanned shutdown, force majeure or production shut-in in 2022-2025. The other dated incidents named are outside the window (2019, 2021). The FY2025 report's events-after-the-reporting-period note lists only financing and a share repurchase. Aramco annual reports are therefore not an incident source for this window.
lanes.limitation: The Tadawul announcement list refused access (HTTP 403) and was not read; neither declared query ran (shared search limit); the Arabic annual reports were not read (English editions only). Aramco's 2026 interim reports and results releases were deliberately not opened: they are outside the declared 2022-2025 annual-report universe and would carry current operating information during the active campaign.

lanes.source_family: GASTAT and JODI production releases (production effects explicitly attributed to a disruption)
lanes.finding: GASTAT does not attribute production changes to a disruption in the releases read. The monthly IPI release is a short bulletin of index movements: it says the index moved 'affected by the decline in mining and quarrying activity' and names the manufacturing sub-activities that moved, but gives no cause for the mining or refining movement (no incident, attack, outage or policy reason) in the two campaign-period months read. JODI-Oil publishes a numeric database with definitions, a manual and availability footnotes only; the pages opened carry no narrative attribution.
lanes.limitation: Only two monthly IPI release PDFs were read in full (March and April 2026, English), so no continuous span is covered and covered_through is null. The 2022-2025 monthly releases, the Arabic editions and GASTAT's petroleum-and-gas statistics were not read, and the search listing did not show a complete 2022-2025 series on the pages opened. JODI's Saudi metadata page was not reached.

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: One automated visit to each cited page. Blocked means the site refused an automated visitor, not that the page is gone. Changed content needs an earlier visit to compare with, so this first run cannot report it.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
